newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-Mexico battles against US corn sweeteners.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Mexico battles against US corn sweeteners.

text.p: In the battle to quench the thirst of Mexican consumers, U.S. forces carry corn syrup, the defenders lob sugar and victory may be decided by the World Trade Organization.

Mexico -- at least demographically -- is a young, thirsty nation. Not only is more than half of its population under the age of 21, but its per capita soft drink consumption is second only to the United States.
Both factors make it an attractive market for U.S. high-fructose corn syrup (HFCS) producers such as Cargill Inc., A.E. Staley Manufacturing Co., CPC International Inc. and Archer Daniels Midland Co.

Fifteen years ago, those companies became dominant in the U.S. soft drink sweetener market. Now Mexican sugar producers, who sell about 35 percent of their sugar to Mexican soft drink bottlers, fear they will be the next to fall.
After U.S. exports of HFCS to Mexico surged to 194,800 tonnes in 1996, Mexico sugar producers complained to their government.
